lines: You say it steadily, and for a heartbeat his certainty flickers.
Your voice shakes on the second word. He hears it.

neutral: "Brave. Brave is what the dead are told they were."

stranger_answers.text: He was weaker than you. That is simply how power works.

agree: "At last, a student who has been listening. Weakness is not a crime, boy, but it is a verdict."

stranger_answers.text: Nobody gave you the right to do this.

agree: "No one gives rights. I took one, and you will see whether it holds."
neutral: "Rights are what the strong have left over. Hold on to yours, if you can."
disagree: "A right nobody grants? Then yours is as thin as his was."

stranger_answers.text: He kept his vows. You have broken every one of yours.

agree: "I broke them gladly, when the gods would not keep theirs."
neutral: "Vows. I made mine to people who were not there when they were needed."
disagree: "Vows are what the weak swear to feel safe. Spare me the sermon."

stranger_answers.text: You have torn something out of this place that will not grow back.

agree: "The valley will grow what it grows. I will not apologise to a hill."
neutral: "Things grow back. People who can do what I do are rarer."
disagree: "Balance is what the powerless call their fear. Spare me the hill-talk."

stranger_answers.text: He taught half this village their trade. What does your grievance pay for that?

agree: "Nothing. And that is the whole of my point: the world has no price for what I will do."
neutral: "A trade, a debt. Everything balances in the end."
disagree: "Count the dead of Harrowmere, then come and talk to me about ledgers."

stranger_answers.text: He had a duty to this village. You had no claim on it at all.

agree: "Duty. Claim. Titles, at last, from a child. I did not expect the word."
neutral: "Perhaps. Claims are made by the one still standing."
disagree: "A claim needs someone to enforce it. Look around you: who is enforcing his?"

stranger_answers.text: ...This feels like a play. These are exactly the lines a villain gives.

agree: "Then you see it too. The pattern. The rooms that repeat. I thought I was alone."
neutral: "If it is a play, it is the only one I can bear to stay in."

challenge_or_not.text: Then prove it. Ward against Ward, here, now.
lines: You lift the staff. The square goes very quiet.

neutral: "...Very well. On the old rules: three colours, three places. Break mine and I will leave. If I break yours, there will be one apprentice fewer, and nobody will remember who you were."

lines: You keep your hands where they are. He waits a moment longer than he needs to, then turns away.

neutral: "Wise. Or frightened. From here they look the same."

pages.speaker: narrator
lines: A stranger in a dark travelling cloak is walking into {settlement} along the road. Nobody has stopped him. Under the cloak, light moves like something alive.

pages.speaker: narrator
lines: {mentor} has stopped what they were doing. The staff that has leaned in the corner of every lesson is in their hand.

pages.speaker: mentor
lines: {attacker}. I had hoped never to see this day. You have grown thin.

pages.speaker: attacker
lines: Thin. Yes. Ten winters of doing what you would not teach me to do. I walked through the blight at Harrowmere while you taught children to light candles. They begged for anyone with power to command the sickness, the lords, anything. Nobody was permitted to. I learned what that costs.

pages.speaker: mentor
lines: And you decided that the answer was to be the one permitted. Power is not a licence, {attacker}. It is what we owe the ones who cannot do what we can.

pages.speaker: attacker
lines: A comforting thing to say with a roof over your head. I came to ask you once more to stand with me. The Weave answers to the strongest. The world should too.

pages.speaker: mentor
lines: No.

pages.speaker: narrator
lines: {attacker} lifts one hand. The light under his cloak opens like a door. {mentor} raises a Ward, a good one, three-fold and old, and it shatters like thin ice.

pages.speaker: narrator
lines: {mentor} falls. The staff rolls across the dirt and lies still. All around the square, people stop and stare.

pages.speaker: narrator
lines: He turns. For the first time he sees you.

lines.text: The apprentice. A child with a borrowed staff. Your teacher was the best of them, and it took me less than a breath.
The apprentice. I hear you have already killed your friend in the road and dragged them back by the heels. Good. So you can be taught, after all; your teacher could not manage it in a season.

The apprentice. I watched you two throwing Wards at each other in the road like children with stones while your teacher waited with the real lesson. {mentor} deserved a better pupil. So, it seems, did I.
The apprentice. You have died already, I am told, and somebody was fool enough to bring you back. Do not count on it twice.
They never even finished teaching you. I can see it in how you hold that staff.
There is more craft in you than your teacher let on. Interesting. It will not be enough.

pages.speaker: attacker
lines: I am not a butcher, and you are not enough: not for me, not yet for anything. Become more. There is a craft older than the schools, and I mean to teach the world what it is for. When you can bear to stand against me, come and find me.

pages.speaker: narrator
lines: The stranger stops in the middle of {settlement} and looks around as if counting the houses. People watch him from doorways and say nothing.

pages.speaker: attacker
lines: I came for my old teacher, {mentor}. I find the village has already buried them and left a child with their staff. Very well.

pages.speaker: narrator
lines: The stranger's Ward breaks, and the light under his cloak gutters out. He staggers and stares at his own open hand as if it belonged to someone else.

pages.speaker: attacker
lines: Lucky. Lucky, and taught by a better teacher than you deserve. This is not finished. There is a craft older than the schools, and I know where it is kept. I will come back when you are able to bear it.

pages.speaker: narrator
lines: He backs away and the cloak closes around him. By the time the square has found its voice again, the road is empty.

pages.speaker: narrator
lines: {mentor} lies where they fell. The settlement is silent; the work has stopped. Then, somewhere, an axe falls again, because trees do not wait for grief. People will want to talk, and you should listen.
